     8→@total_ordering
     9→class _Condition:
    10→    def __init__(self, operator, version):
    11→        self.operator = operator
    12→        self.display_version = version
    13→
    14→        value = str(version)
    15→        if (operator == ">=" or operator == "<") and "-" not in value:
    16→            value += "-"
    17→        self.version = Version(value)
    18→
    19→    def __str__(self):
    20→        return f"{self.operator}{self.display_version}"
    21→
    22→    def __repr__(self):
    23→        return self.__str__()
    24→
    25→    def __hash__(self):
    26→        return hash((self.operator, self.version))
    27→
    28→    def __lt__(self, other):
    29→        # Notice that this is done on the modified version, might contain extra prereleases
    30→        if self.version < other.version:
    31→            return True
    32→        elif self.version == other.version:
    33→            if self.operator == "<":
    34→                if other.operator == "<":
    35→                    return self.display_version.pre is not None
    36→                else:
    37→                    return True
    38→            elif self.operator == "<=":
    39→                if other.operator == "<":
    40→                    return False
    41→                else:
    42→                    return self.display_version.pre is None
    43→            elif self.operator == ">":
    44→                if other.operator == ">":
    45→                    return self.display_version.pre is None
    46→                else:
    47→                    return False
    48→            else:
    49→                if other.operator == ">":
    50→                    return True
    51→                # There's a possibility of getting here while validating if a range is non-void
    52→                # by comparing >= & <= for lower limit <= upper limit
    53→                elif other.operator == "<=":
    54→                    return True
    55→                else:
    56→                    return self.display_version.pre is not None
    57→        return False
    58→
    59→    def __eq__(self, other):
    60→        return (self.display_version == other.display_version and
    61→                self.operator == other.operator)

    64→class _ConditionSet:
    65→
    66→    def __init__(self, expression, prerelease):
    67→        expressions = expression.split()
    68→        self.prerelease = prerelease
    69→        self.conditions = []
    70→        for e in expressions:
    71→            e = e.strip()
    72→            self.conditions.extend(self._parse_expression(e))
    73→
    74→    @staticmethod
    75→    def _parse_expression(expression):
    76→        if expression in ("", "*"):
    77→            return [_Condition(">=", Version("0.0.0"))]
    78→        elif len(expression) == 1:
    79→            raise ConanException(f'Error parsing version range "{expression}"')
    80→
    81→        operator = expression[0]
    82→        if operator not in (">", "<", "^", "~", "="):
    83→            operator = "="
    84→            index = 0
    85→        else:
    86→            index = 1
    87→        if operator in (">", "<"):
    88→            if expression[1] == "=":
    89→                operator += "="
    90→                index = 2
    91→        version = expression[index:]
    92→        if version == "":
    93→            raise ConanException(f'Error parsing version range "{expression}"')
    94→        if operator == "~":  # tilde minor
    95→            if "-" not in version:
    96→                version += "-"
    97→            v = Version(version)
    98→            index = 1 if len(v.main) > 1 else 0
    99→            return [_Condition(">=", v), _Condition("<", v.upper_bound(index))]
   100→        elif operator == "^":  # caret major
   101→            v = Version(version)
   102→
   103→            def first_non_zero(main):
   104→                for i, m in enumerate(main):
   105→                    if m != 0:
   106→                        return i
   107→                return len(main)
   108→
   109→            initial_index = first_non_zero(v.main)
   110→            return [_Condition(">=", v), _Condition("<", v.upper_bound(initial_index))]
   111→        else:
   112→            return [_Condition(operator, Version(version))]
   113→
   114→    def _valid(self, version, conf_resolve_prepreleases):
   115→        if version.pre:
   116→            # Follow the expression desires only if core.version_ranges:resolve_prereleases is None,
   117→            # else force to the conf's value
   118→            if conf_resolve_prepreleases is None:
   119→                if not self.prerelease:
   120→                    return False
   121→            elif conf_resolve_prepreleases is False:
   122→                return False
   123→        for condition in self.conditions:
   124→            if condition.operator == ">":
   125→                if not version > condition.version:
   126→                    return False
   127→            elif condition.operator == "<":
   128→                if not version < condition.version:
   129→                    return False
   130→            elif condition.operator == ">=":
   131→                if not version >= condition.version:
   132→                    return False
   133→            elif condition.operator == "<=":
   134→                if not version <= condition.version:
   135→                    return False
   136→            elif condition.operator == "=":
   137→                if not version == condition.version:
   138→                    return False
   139→        return True

   142→class VersionRange:
   143→    def __init__(self, expression):
   144→        self._expression = expression
   145→        tokens = expression.split(",")
   146→        prereleases = False
   147→        for t in tokens[1:]:
   148→            if "include_prerelease" in t:
   149→                if "include_prerelease=" in t:
   150→                    from conan.api.output import ConanOutput
   151→                    ConanOutput().warning(
   152→                        f'include_prerelease version range option in "{expression}" does not take an attribute, '
   153→                        'its presence unconditionally enables prereleases')
   154→                prereleases = True
   155→                break
   156→            else:
   157→                t = t.strip()
   158→                if len(t) > 0 and t[0].isalpha():
   159→                    from conan.api.output import ConanOutput
   160→                    ConanOutput().warning(f'Unrecognized version range option "{t}" in "{expression}"')
   161→                else:
   162→                    raise ConanException(f'"{t}" in version range "{expression}" is not a valid option')
   163→        version_expr = tokens[0]
   164→        self.condition_sets = []
   165→        for alternative in version_expr.split("||"):
   166→            self.condition_sets.append(_ConditionSet(alternative, prereleases))
   167→
   168→    def __str__(self):
   169→        return self._expression
   170→
   171→    def contains(self, version: Version, resolve_prerelease: Optional[bool]):
   172→        """
   173→        Whether <version> is inside the version range
   174→
   175→        :param version: Version to check against
   176→        :param resolve_prerelease: If ``True``, ensure prereleases can be resolved in this range
   177→        If ``False``, prerelases can NOT be resolved in this range
   178→        If ``None``, prereleases are resolved only if this version range expression says so
   179→        :return: Whether the version is inside the range
   180→        """
   181→        assert isinstance(version, Version), type(version)
   182→        for condition_set in self.condition_sets:
   183→            if condition_set._valid(version, resolve_prerelease):
   184→                return True
   185→        return False
   186→
   187→    def intersection(self, other):
   188→        conditions = []
   189→
   190→        def _calculate_limits(operator, lhs, rhs):
   191→            limits = ([c for c in lhs.conditions if operator in c.operator]
   192→                      + [c for c in rhs.conditions if operator in c.operator])
   193→            if limits:
   194→                return sorted(limits, reverse=operator == ">")[0]
   195→
   196→        for lhs_conditions in self.condition_sets:
   197→            for rhs_conditions in other.condition_sets:
   198→                internal_conditions = []
   199→                lower_limit = _calculate_limits(">", lhs_conditions, rhs_conditions)
   200→                upper_limit = _calculate_limits("<", lhs_conditions, rhs_conditions)
   201→                if lower_limit:
   202→                    internal_conditions.append(lower_limit)
   203→                if upper_limit:
   204→                    internal_conditions.append(upper_limit)
   205→                if internal_conditions and (not lower_limit or not upper_limit or lower_limit <= upper_limit):
   206→                    conditions.append(internal_conditions)
   207→
   208→        if not conditions:
   209→            return None
   210→        expression = ' || '.join(' '.join(str(c) for c in cs) for cs in conditions)
   211→        result = VersionRange(expression)
   212→        # TODO: Direct definition of conditions not reparsing
   213→        # result.condition_sets = self.condition_sets + other.condition_sets
   214→        return result
   215→
   216→    def version(self):
   217→        return Version(f"[{self._expression}]")
   218→

     6→@total_ordering
     7→class _VersionItem:
     8→    """ a single "digit" in a version, like X.Y.Z all X and Y and Z are VersionItems
     9→    They can be int or strings
    10→    """
    11→    def __init__(self, item):
    12→        try:
    13→            self._v = int(item)
    14→        except ValueError:
    15→            self._v = item
    16→
    17→    @property
    18→    def value(self):
    19→        return self._v
    20→
    21→    def __str__(self):
    22→        return str(self._v)
    23→
    24→    def __add__(self, other):
    25→        # necessary for the "bump()" functionality. Other aritmetic operations are missing
    26→        return self._v + other
    27→
    28→    def __eq__(self, other):
    29→        if not isinstance(other, _VersionItem):
    30→            other = _VersionItem(other)
    31→        return self._v == other._v
    32→
    33→    def __hash__(self):
    34→        return hash(self._v)
    35→
    36→    def __lt__(self, other):
    37→        """
    38→        @type other: _VersionItem
    39→        """
    40→        if not isinstance(other, _VersionItem):
    41→            other = _VersionItem(other)
    42→        try:
    43→            return self._v < other._v
    44→        except TypeError:
    45→            return str(self._v) < str(other._v)

    48→@total_ordering
    49→class Version:
    50→    """
    51→    This is NOT an implementation of semver, as users may use any pattern in their versions.
    52→    It is just a helper to parse "." or "-" and compare taking into account integers when possible
    53→    """
    54→    def __init__(self, value, qualifier=False):
    55→        value = str(value)
    56→        self._value = value
    57→        self._build = None
    58→        self._pre = None
    59→        self._qualifier = qualifier  # it is a prerelease or build qualifier, not a main version
    60→
    61→        if not qualifier:
    62→            items = value.rsplit("+", 1)  # split for build
    63→            if len(items) == 2:
    64→                value, build = items
    65→                self._build = Version(build, qualifier=True)  # This is a nested version by itself
    66→
    67→            # split for pre-release, from the left, semver allows hyphens in identifiers :(
    68→            items = value.split("-", 1)
    69→            if len(items) == 2:
    70→                value, pre = items
    71→                self._pre = Version(pre, qualifier=True)  # This is a nested version by itself
    72→
    73→        items = value.split(".")
    74→        items = [_VersionItem(item) for item in items]
    75→        self._items = tuple(items)
    76→        while items and items[-1].value == 0:
    77→            del items[-1]
    78→        self._nonzero_items = tuple(items)
    79→
    80→    def bump(self, index):
    81→        """
    82→        :meta private:
    83→            Bump the version
    84→            Increments by 1 the version field at the specified index, setting to 0 the fields
    85→            on the right.
    86→            2.5 => bump(1) => 2.6
    87→            1.5.7 => bump(0) => 2.0.0
    88→
    89→        :param index:
    90→        """
    91→        # this method is used to compute version ranges from tilde ~1.2 and caret ^1.2.1 ranges
    92→        # TODO: at this moment it only works for digits, cannot increment pre-release or builds
    93→        # better not make it public yet, keep it internal
    94→        items = list(self._items[:index])
    95→        try:
    96→            items.append(self._items[index]+1)
    97→        except TypeError:
    98→            raise ConanException(f"Cannot bump '{self._value} version index {index}, not an int")
    99→        items.extend([0] * (len(items) - index - 1))
   100→        v = ".".join(str(i) for i in items)
   101→        # prerelease and build are dropped while bumping digits
   102→        return Version(v)
   103→
   104→    def upper_bound(self, index):
   105→        items = list(self._items[:index])
   106→        try:
   107→            items.append(self._items[index] + 1)
   108→        except TypeError:
   109→            raise ConanException(f"Cannot bump '{self._value} version index {index}, not an int")
   110→        items.extend([0] * (len(items) - index - 1))
   111→        v = ".".join(str(i) for i in items)
   112→        v += "-"  # Exclude prereleases
   113→        return Version(v)
   114→
   115→    @property
   116→    def pre(self):
   117→        return self._pre
   118→
   119→    @property
   120→    def build(self):
   121→        return self._build
   122→
   123→    @property
   124→    def main(self):
   125→        return self._items
   126→
   127→    @property
   128→    def major(self):
   129→        try:
   130→            return self.main[0]
   131→        except IndexError:
   132→            return None
   133→
   134→    @property
   135→    def minor(self):
   136→        try:
   137→            return self.main[1]
   138→        except IndexError:
   139→            return None
   140→
   141→    @property
   142→    def patch(self):
   143→        try:
   144→            return self.main[2]
   145→        except IndexError:
   146→            return None
   147→
   148→    @property
   149→    def micro(self):
   150→        try:
   151→            return self.main[3]
   152→        except IndexError:
   153→            return None
   154→
   155→    def __str__(self):
   156→        return self._value
   157→
   158→    def __repr__(self):
   159→        return self._value
   160→
   161→    def __eq__(self, other):
   162→        if other is None:
   163→            return False
   164→        if not isinstance(other, Version):
   165→            other = Version(other, self._qualifier)
   166→
   167→        return (self._nonzero_items, self._pre, self._build) ==\
   168→               (other._nonzero_items, other._pre, other._build)
   169→
   170→    def __hash__(self):
   171→        return hash((self._nonzero_items, self._pre, self._build))
   172→
   173→    def __lt__(self, other):
   174→        if other is None:
   175→            return False
   176→        if not isinstance(other, Version):
   177→            other = Version(other)
   178→
   179→        if self._pre:
   180→            if other._pre:  # both are pre-releases
   181→                return (self._nonzero_items, self._pre, self._build) < \
   182→                       (other._nonzero_items, other._pre, other._build)
   183→            else:  # Left hand is pre-release, right side is regular
   184→                if self._nonzero_items == other._nonzero_items:  # Problem only happens if both equal
   185→                    return True
   186→                else:
   187→                    return self._nonzero_items < other._nonzero_items
   188→        else:
   189→            if other._pre:  # Left hand is regular, right side is pre-release
   190→                if self._nonzero_items == other._nonzero_items:  # Problem only happens if both equal
   191→                    return False
   192→                else:
   193→                    return self._nonzero_items < other._nonzero_items
   194→            else:  # None of them is pre-release
   195→                return (self._nonzero_items, self._build) < (other._nonzero_items, other._build)
   196→

     7→class VersionReprTest(unittest.TestCase):
     8→
     9→    def test_text(self):
    10→        v1 = Version("master+build2")
    11→        vr = _VersionRepr(v1)
    12→        assert vr.major() == "master"
    13→        assert vr.minor() == "master"
    14→        assert vr.patch() == "master"
    15→        assert vr.pre() == "master"
    16→        assert vr.build == "build2"
    17→        assert vr.stable() == "master"
    18→
    19→    def test_patch(self):
    20→        v1 = Version("1.2.3-alpha1+build2")
    21→        vr = _VersionRepr(v1)
    22→        assert vr.major() == "1.Y.Z"
    23→        assert vr.minor() == "1.2.Z"
    24→        assert vr.patch() == "1.2.3"
    25→        assert vr.pre() == "1.2.3-alpha1"
    26→        assert vr.build == "build2"
    27→        assert vr.stable() == "1.Y.Z"
    28→
    29→        v1 = Version("1.2.3+build2")
    30→        vr = _VersionRepr(v1)
    31→        self.assertEqual(vr.major(), "1.Y.Z")
    32→        self.assertEqual(vr.minor(), "1.2.Z")
    33→        self.assertEqual(vr.patch(), "1.2.3")
    34→        self.assertEqual(vr.pre(), "1.2.3")
    35→        self.assertEqual(vr.build, "build2")
    36→        self.assertEqual(vr.stable(), "1.Y.Z")
    37→
    38→        v1 = Version("0.2.3-alpha1+build2")
    39→        vr = _VersionRepr(v1)
    40→        self.assertEqual(vr.major(), "0.Y.Z")
    41→        self.assertEqual(vr.minor(), "0.2.Z")
    42→        self.assertEqual(vr.patch(), "0.2.3")
    43→        self.assertEqual(vr.pre(), "0.2.3-alpha1")
    44→        self.assertEqual(vr.build, "build2")
    45→        self.assertEqual(vr.stable(), "0.2.3-alpha1+build2")
    46→
    47→        v1 = Version("+build2")
    48→        vr = _VersionRepr(v1)
    49→        assert vr.major() == ""
    50→
    51→    def test_build(self):
    52→        v1 = Version("0.2.3-alpha1+build2")
    53→        vr = _VersionRepr(v1)
    54→        self.assertEqual(vr.build, "build2")
    55→        v2 = Version("0.2.3+b178")
    56→        vr = _VersionRepr(v2)
    57→        self.assertEqual(vr.build, "b178")

    11→@total_ordering
    12→class RecipeReference:
    13→    """ an exact (no version-range, no alias) reference of a recipe.
    14→    Should be enough to locate a recipe in the cache or in a server
    15→    Validation will be external to this class, at specific points (export, api, etc)
    16→    """
    17→
    18→    def __init__(self, name=None, version=None, user=None, channel=None, revision=None,
    19→                 timestamp=None):
    20→        self.name = name
    21→        if version is not None and not isinstance(version, Version):
    22→            version = Version(version)
    23→        self.version = version  # This MUST be a version if we want to be able to order
    24→        self.user = user
    25→        self.channel = channel
    26→        self.revision = revision
    27→        self.timestamp = timestamp
    28→
    29→    def __repr__(self):
    30→        """ long repr like pkg/0.1@user/channel#rrev%timestamp """
    31→        result = self.repr_notime()
    32→        if self.timestamp is not None:
    33→            result += "%{}".format(self.timestamp)
    34→        return result
    35→
    36→    def repr_notime(self):
    37→        result = self.__str__()
    38→        if self.revision is not None:
    39→            result += "#{}".format(self.revision)
    40→        return result
    41→
    42→    def repr_reduced(self):
    43→        result = self.__str__()
    44→        if self.revision is not None:
    45→            result += "#{}".format(self.revision[0:4])
    46→        return result
    47→
    48→    def repr_humantime(self):
    49→        result = self.repr_notime()
    50→        assert self.timestamp
    51→        result += " ({})".format(timestamp_to_str(self.timestamp))
    52→        return result
    53→
    54→    def __str__(self):
    55→        """ shorter representation, excluding the revision and timestamp """
    56→        if self.name is None:
    57→            return ""
    58→        result = "/".join([self.name, str(self.version)])
    59→        if self.user:
    60→            result += "@{}".format(self.user)
    61→        if self.channel:
    62→            assert self.user
    63→            result += "/{}".format(self.channel)
    64→        return result
    65→
    66→    def __lt__(self, ref):
    67→        # The timestamp goes before the revision for ordering revisions chronologically
    68→        # In theory this is enough for sorting
    69→        # When no timestamp is given, it will always have lower priority, to avoid comparison
    70→        # errors float <> None
    71→        return (self.name, self.version, self.user or "", self.channel or "", self.timestamp or 0,
    72→                self.revision or "") \
    73→               < (ref.name, ref.version, ref.user or "", ref.channel or "", ref.timestamp or 0,
    74→                  ref.revision or "")
    75→
    76→    def __eq__(self, ref):
    77→        # Timestamp doesn't affect equality.
    78→        # This is necessary for building an ordered list of UNIQUE recipe_references for Lockfile
    79→        if ref is None:
    80→            return False
    81→        # If one revision is not defined, they are equal
    82→        if self.revision is not None and ref.revision is not None:
    83→            return (self.name, self.version, self.user, self.channel, self.revision) == \
    84→                   (ref.name, ref.version, ref.user, ref.channel, ref.revision)
    85→        return (self.name, self.version, self.user, self.channel) == \
    86→               (ref.name, ref.version, ref.user, ref.channel)
    87→
    88→    def __hash__(self):
    89→        # This is necessary for building an ordered list of UNIQUE recipe_references for Lockfile
    90→        return hash((self.name, self.version, self.user, self.channel))
    91→
    92→    @staticmethod
    93→    def loads(rref):
    94→        try:
    95→            # timestamp
    96→            tokens = rref.rsplit("%", 1)
    97→            text = tokens[0]
    98→            timestamp = float(tokens[1]) if len(tokens) == 2 else None
    99→
   100→            # revision
   101→            tokens = text.split("#", 1)
   102→            ref = tokens[0]
   103→            revision = tokens[1] if len(tokens) == 2 else None
   104→
   105→            # name, version always here
   106→            tokens = ref.split("@", 1)
   107→            name, version = tokens[0].split("/", 1)
   108→            assert name and version
   109→            # user and channel
   110→            if len(tokens) == 2 and tokens[1]:
   111→                tokens = tokens[1].split("/", 1)
   112→                user = tokens[0] if tokens[0] else None
   113→                channel = tokens[1] if len(tokens) == 2 else None
   114→            else:
   115→                user = channel = None
   116→            return RecipeReference(name, version, user, channel, revision, timestamp)
   117→        except Exception:
   118→            from conans.errors import ConanException
   119→            raise ConanException(
   120→                f"{rref} is not a valid recipe reference, provide a reference"

text: Plan: - Investigate how version ranges are parsed and compared, focusing on handling of build metadata (+). - Write a unit test reproducing the reported failure for ranges like >=1.0.0+2. - Find the root cause in version range parsing. - Implement a fix to properly handle build metadata when appending a “-” to exclude prereleases. - Run unit tests to validate the fix. Summary of investigation: - Conan’s Version class (conans/model/version.py) is not pure semver: it compares main parts, prerelease, and build, and build metadata participates in ordering. - VersionRange (conans/model/version_range.py) modifies the boundary values in _Condition.__init__ by appending a “-” to exclude prereleases when the operator is >= or <: value = str(version) if (operator == ">=" or operator == "<") and "-" not in value: value += "-" - This logic breaks for values that include build metadata, e.g., "1.0.0+2". Appending "-" produces "1.0.0+2-", which incorrectly turns the build portion into “2-” (a qualifier version), altering comparisons and preventing correct resolution for ranges like ">=1.0.0+2". Reproduction tests added: - Added tests that demonstrate the expected behavior for ranges with build metadata: File: conans/test/unittests/model/version/test_version_range.py - New tests at the end: def test_build_metadata_in_greater_equal_range(): r = VersionRange('>=1.0.0+2') assert r.contains(Version('1.0.0+2'), None) assert not r.contains(Version('1.0.0+1'), None) def test_build_metadata_in_less_than_range(): r = VersionRange('<1.0.0+2') assert r.contains(Version('1.0.0+1'), None) assert not r.contains(Version('1.0.0+2'), None) Root cause: - The code unconditionally appends "-" for >= and < operations, even if the string contains "+". This inserts the "-" into the build metadata, effectively creating a malformed boundary version and enabling or disabling versions incorrectly. Fix implemented: - In conans/model/version_range.py, update _Condition.__init__ to avoid appending "-" when the value contains "+" (build metadata), because build metadata already participates in comparisons and we shouldn’t convert the bound into a prerelease: Old: if (operator == ">=" or operator == "<") and "-" not in value: value += "-" New: if (operator == ">=" or operator == "<") and "-" not in value: # Append '-' to exclude prereleases only when no build metadata is present. # If '+' (build metadata) exists, do NOT append '-', because build metadata # participates in comparison in Conan and adding '-' would incorrectly # turn the bound into a prerelease and allow older builds. if "+" not in value: value += "-" This preserves existing behavior for plain versions (exclude prereleases when appropriate) while correctly handling versions with build metadata. Validation: - Ran the specific unit tests for version ranges: pytest -q conans/test/unittests/model/version/test_version_range.py -q All tests passed, including the newly added build metadata tests. - Also ran intersection tests: pytest -q conans/test/unittests/model/version/test_version_range.py conans/test/unittests/model/version/test_version_range_intersection.py -q All tests passed. Notes: - Running the entire test suite in this environment hit a Python 3.6 issue unrelated to this change (importing SortKey from pstats). I limited runs to the relevant unit tests which passed successfully. - I did not make any commits, as requested. - The new tests are proper unit tests that validate expected behavior and are not temporary files. If you prefer not to include new tests in the repo, let me know and I can remove them after verification. How this fixes your scenario: - With the fix, requiring self.requires("package/[>=1.0.0+2]") will evaluate the >= bound correctly against a package version 1.0.0+2 and select it, while rejecting 1.0.0+1. It will not mistakenly transform the bound into something like "1.0.0+2-" which previously caused resolution failures.
